sentences.text: In 2023, this party came first in Spain. But this man became prime minister. How?
Who can vote? Spaniards from 18, even those living abroad.
You get two ballots. For Congress, you pick one party's list, with no changes, and drop it in the envelope.
Each province shares its seats among parties above 3%.
For the Senate, you tick up to three candidates.
The 350 members of Congress make the laws and elect the prime minister. The Senate can amend them, but Congress has the last word.
The People's Party won 137 seats, short of the 176 needed.
Its leader, Feijóo, lost the vote. Pedro Sánchez of the Socialists won it, backed by Sumar and regional parties.
And the King? Felipe the Sixth inherited the throne. He proposes the candidate and signs every law, but can't block one.
Should the party with the most votes always get to govern?
